statements.status_notes: Scanners report pkg:pypi/msgpack@1.1.2 from the copy pip vendors under pip/_vendor/msgpack (listed in pip/_vendor/vendor.txt). This image installs no standalone msgpack distribution, and pip's vendored copy is pure Python only (__init__.py, exceptions.py, ext.py, fallback.py), with no msgpack._cmsgpack C extension. CVE-2026-114613 (GHSA-j586-36cw-2gc2) covers a map-value leak when strict_map_key rejects a key and a stale parser-stack reference in the streaming Unpacker, both in the C sources (msgpack/unpack.h, msgpack/unpack_template.h) that build msgpack._cmsgpack; the pure-Python fallback checks the key before decoding the value and does not contain that code.

Scanners report pkg:pypi/msgpack@1.1.2 from pip's vendored copy under pip/_vendor/msgpack (vendor.txt and bom.cdx.json). NiFi consumes the DHI Debian Python base image, which ships pip's pure-Python msgpack fallback only (__init__.py, exceptions.py, ext.py, fallback.py); there is no msgpack._cmsgpack C extension in that tree. CVE-2026-114613 is an unbounded memory leak in the C extension when strict_map_key rejects a map key; upstream and Debian document that the pure-Python fallback does not exhibit this leak.

msgpack 1.1.2 appears in the SBOM as a cataloger artifact sourced from jupyter_client's test-extra dependency declaration in its METADATA file. The package is not installed in the /opt/singleuser/.venv Python environment and cannot be imported at runtime. The vulnerable code is not present in the running container.

Alias of CVE-2026-57585. pip vendors msgpack 1.1.2 without the vulnerable _cmsgpack C extension; only the pure-Python fallback is present under pip/_vendor/msgpack.

pip's vendored msgpack is the pure-Python fallback only (fallback.py, ext.py, exceptions.py). CVE-2026-57585 is a use-after-free in the Cython _cmsgpack extension; pip does not ship that native module and always falls back to the pure-Python implementation.
